fixed_source.result_applied: Theorem H (two physical hubs, diagonal light block) applied to the target-valid aligned Hadamard star, giving continuous density <=4/L while every physical pair misses L/64 and Xi=0

new_claims.statement: For any two-row arm M, symmetric same-bank S and physical K, det(M_KM_K^T)||S[Kc,K](I-P_K)||F^2 equals the sum of squared 3x3 determinants det([M_T;S[i,T]])^2 over i outside K and triples T inside K; Bernoulli p=3/4 gives expectation (27/256)Xi.

In the full two-hub common-plane geometry, some physical cut either gives continuous density <=2^(13/6)sqrt(3) Xi^(-1/6), retaining arbitrary cross-tail and same-bank terms, or produces a physical row carrying more than half the projected crossing mass.
Xi(M,S)=S_M^2 D_M(S)^2 exactly, where D_M(S)^2=sum_i(1-ell_i)dist(S[i,-i],row(M_-i))^2; the diffuse receiver is 7.776645188958661(S_M D_M)^(-1/3).

With inherited arm area S_M>L^2/(64sqrt(896)), D_M>=0.003798734015533447 L is either paid by <619/L or gives an actual projected row >8.7234000062e-4 L. If arm leverages <=1/2 and unpaid/nonlocalized, total leave-one-out misalignment is <0.005372221164615409 L.
When every arm leverage is <1, D_M(S)=0 iff S=M^T R M+D with R symmetric 2x2 and D physical diagonal.

A two-bank Hadamard star has spectrum {+L,+L,-L,-L}, every physical pair below L/64 for m>=4096, diffuse arms, and Xi=0. It refutes any claim that the target spectrum forces positive compound currency; fixed-source Theorem H nevertheless gives continuous density <=4/L for arbitrary cap-one product sources.
